name: MaleCNS connectome topology benchmarks
description: This dataset supports evaluation of MaleCNS v1.0 Drosophila connectivity as a fixed edge pattern in trainable sparse recurrent networks. It combines derived physiological forecasting data from VitalDB with selected connectome subgraphs, matched graph controls, trained models, and saved predictions. The processed physiological dataset contains 476,544 windows from 3,357 surgical cases and 3,253 subjects. Inputs are 60-s histories of invasive mean arterial pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, and end-tidal carbon dioxide, sampled on a 2-s grid. The target is mean arterial pressure averaged over a 60-s future interval beginning 300 s after the history ends. The subject-disjoint test set contains 74,187 windows from 484 subjects. The graph collection contains biological subgraphs of 256, 512, and 1,024 nodes at synaptic-count thresholds of 1 and 5, together with 30 null graphs. Node tables map model indices to source neuron body identifiers. Degree-preserving controls retain each node's incoming and outgoing degree; edge-matched random controls retain node and edge counts. The main trained biological network uses the binary threshold-5 topology with 1,024 nodes and 27,789 recurrent edges. The package includes 65 model checkpoints and prediction files, per-run metrics and training histories, cohort/QC tables, configuration and source code, node manifests, body-mapped edge exports, graph audits, and reproduction utilities.
